_about: Rules for app/claims: how a claim sheet (a PDF of it, or a scanned picture of it) is read. Every word is matched in lower case with spaces collapsed. Decided with the owner 2026-09-24 (blueprint section 6, decisions D24-D26).
_date_headers: The header of the date column (the whole header cell, not part of it).
_expense_columns: The expense columns by name. A column is recognised when its header holds every listed word as a whole word.
_expense_range: Every non-zero amount in the columns from the first to the last named here (both included) is one claim item, whatever the columns in between are called, so a column added to the form is never skipped (owner, D24, D40). Without both ends on the sheet, the named columns alone count.
_min_expense_columns: A table is a claim table only when its header row holds the date header and at least this many expense columns.
_total_headers: The row-total column: a header cell equal to one of these, or starting with 'total:' (e.g. 'Total:USD').
_rows: The data rows end at the first row holding a total-row label (the grand Total is read there) or a stop label.
_header_block: Rows right under the header row belong to the header when every filled cell is text or a ledger code (a whole number of at least ledger_code_min_digits digits, e.g. 4740150) - so codes never become claims.
_empty_marks: Cell text that means 'nothing' (Excel shows a zero as '-').
_currency_codes: Shown with the grand totals when the sheet's header names one. Not used to match anything.
_ocr_digit_repairs: In a date written in digits, these letters next to a digit or a separator are read as digits (OCR of a scanned sheet).
_dates: Claim-sheet dates, rule R10u (owner, 2026-09-24; tools/date_parsing_trial): each cell's possible readings; per sheet, a date with a part above 12 fixes the order, then no reading after the day of checking, then the order keeping the sheet within max_claim_span_days; still open -> the receipts decide (app/checking), else the officer.
_pdf_min_text_words: A PDF page with fewer words in its text layer is treated as a picture (read by OCR).
_pdf_lines: Table lines drawn in a PDF: segments at least this long, positions within cluster_pt counted as one line, bands thinner than min_band_pt (double borders) dropped.
_image_lines: Table lines in a scanned sheet: dark strokes at least this share of the page width (horizontal) / height (vertical) long - vertical ones longer than any digit - found by morphological opening on an adaptive threshold.
